voice.name: Fiamma
voice.note: clear warm English, neutral — rector's educated daughter, framed at her 1750 letter

segments.e_open: My father knocked on the nursery wall — his own pattern, one nobody else knew. [pause] It knocked back. The same pattern. Knock for knock.
segments.e_s1: The maid heard it first, at the dining-room door. Groans — like a person at the point of death. We laughed at her. [soft laugh] Then the knocking. Three, and a stop, and three again. It came to every one of us in turn.
segments.e_s2: Noises a house cannot make. Several people walking over our heads — running the stairs. All the bottles under the stairs dashed to a thousand pieces — my mother's words, in her letter. And nothing broken. Nothing moved. [pause] Our mastiff whimpered the first night. After that, it hid before the noises began. The dog knew before we did.
segments.e_s3: It interrupted prayers — always at the prayer for the King. Those words, and no others. So my father stood in the nursery and called it out — thou deaf and dumb devil, why dost thou fright these children? Come to me in my study, that am a man. [pause] The next evening, his study door was flung against him. Hard.
segments.e_s4: My sister Hetty trembled in her sleep before the knocks came — it followed her more than any of us. Something went down the stairs in the dark — like a man, in a loose gown, trailing behind him. And my sister Nancy... [pause] Nancy was lifted. Up. With the bed she sat upon.
segments.e_s5: It ended at the end of January — gone, like a guest that had said what it came to say. [pause] Thirty years on, my brother John gathered what we each remembered. I called it 'that wonderful thing called by us Jeffery'. I was four and twenty when it walked our stairs. Not my mother, not my father, not one of my sisters ever took back a word. Neither do I. Make of us what you will.

small: The witness is the rector's eldest daughter.

big: None of them ever took it back.

yt_title: Epworth: It Answered Knock for Knock
